candidate.title: Ig-seq / Rep-Seq / MAF
candidate.scope: The single, grouped Illumina antibody-repertoire schematic, from extracted V–D–J–constant-region RNA through reverse transcription, second strand synthesis, PCR and purification to DNA. The separate CDR3 junction region icon identifies the biological sequence target; it is not a depicted DNA-to-RNA extraction route. The matching secondary catalogue explicitly identifies the two-UID illustration as MAF, and the primary paper calls its workflow Ig-seq with MAF. Thus the drawn route is resolved as the MAF implementation of Ig-seq within Rep-Seq, not as three interchangeable complete protocols. At primary-paper scope it represents mouse IgG heavy-chain transcripts. No separate gDNA Ig-seq route, T-cell receptor workflow, native heavy/light-chain pairing workflow, pooling branch, sequencing operation or computational pipeline is drawn. The adjacent TN-Seq/INSeq, TC-Seq, SSB-Seq rows and chemical structure at the right are outside the assigned row. Source captions and 8N UID symbols are retained; primary-supported interpretations of multiplex tagging and UID chemistry are explicit below.

states.label: Extracted immunoglobulin RNA
features: RNA bearing rearranged V, D and J sequence followed by a constant-region segment, as labeled in the drawing; the CDR3 junction is the highlighted repertoire target.

This is an RNA-derived library architecture. The MAF implementation used to resolve it starts with mouse IgG transcripts; it does not establish the same primer interface for every receptor or specimen.

operations.label: Reverse transcription
operations.description: Copy the immunoglobulin RNA into first-strand cDNA using the depicted tailed primer. The output differs from the input by being a DNA copy with an attached primer-derived reverse UID and partial sequencing adapter; this is not direct genomic-DNA amplification.
operations.mechanism: RNA-templated DNA synthesis initiated at the IgG constant-region-specific primer interface in the paper-resolved MAF implementation. The diagram’s 8N UID label is preserved; the paper specifies an RID with spacers and partial degeneracy.
operations.information_effect: Links antibody transcript identity to an RID in cDNA before multiplex amplification, allowing descendants of a transcript-derived molecule to be associated downstream.

operations.information_effect: Retains the transcript-derived RID while introducing FID diversity that records amplification history. More extensively amplified molecules can receive more FIDs, enabling later bias correction rather than treating both UIDs as equivalent transcript counters.

operations.description: Amplify the dual-tagged antibody DNA into library amplicons. method_scopes.rationale: Applies specifically to Ig-seq performed with MAF in this grouped schematic. Khan et al. explicitly call Fig. 2 Ig-seq with MAF, and describe the same RT → multiplex tagging → adapter extension architecture. This supplies implementation-level evidence beyond the umbrella name. The matched Vollmers reference separately supports an RNA molecule-barcode Ig-seq approach at abstract level; it does not establish the second FID-tagging operation or make its complete protocol identical to MAF. The catalogue’s separate prose description of gDNA Ig-seq is not assigned to any of these RNA/RID-history-dependent local operations, including downstream PCR. The antibody-sequencing review confirms that Ig-seq can use gDNA or mRNA.
